# BINDING CONSISTENCY LEDGER — CANADIAN FRENCH LISTENING POD

## 1. TRANSLITERATION
Not needed — names stay as written.

---

## 2. PRICES
- 8 pound 40 → dix-sept piasses cinquante
- 12 pound 50 → vingt-six piasses

---

## 3. TARGET-LANGUAGE NAME
Canadian French = le français québécois (or *le québécois* in casual speech)

---

## 4. RECURRING LINES

| Canonical | Canadian French |
|-----------|-----------------|
| Good morning / Good afternoon / Good evening. What can I get you? | Bonjour! Qu'est-ce que je peux te servir? |
| Please / With milk but with no sugar. To take away. | S'il te plaît. / Du lait mais pas de sucre. Pour emporter. |
| Thank you very much. Goodbye. | Merci beaucoup. Bonne journée! |
| Excuse me. | Excuse-moi. |
| Could I pay by card? Do you have contactless? | Je pourrais payer avec ma carte? T'as du sans contact? |
| Of course. | Bien sûr. |
| Would you like to sit-in or takeaway? | Tu veux rester ou c'est pour emporter? |
| Yes, of course. | Oui, bien sûr. |
| I'm learning Canadian French. Could you say that again more slowly? | Je suis en train d'apprendre le français québécois. Tu pourrais répéter ça plus lentement, s'il te plaît? |
| Thank you very much, and goodbye. | Merci beaucoup, et bonne journée! |
| You're welcome. | De rien. |
| Yes, I'm on holiday / I'm on holiday here. | Oui, je suis en vacances. |

---

## 5. REGISTER

| Relationship | Address Level | Unmarked Phrasing |
|--------------|---------------|-------------------|
| Barista, cashier, server, shop assistant, pharmacist | *tu* | *Tu veux...?* / *Je peux te servir?* / *S'il te plaît* |
| Stranger (Tourist, Local, Passenger, Driver, Receptionist, Waiter at formal restaurant) | *tu* (default) | *Tu saurais comment...?* / *Tu pourrais...?* / *Si t'as une seconde...* |
| Friend, peer | *tu* | *T'as...?* / *Tu veux...?* / *Ça va?* |
| Elderly neighbour (Scene 1, Scene 5) | *tu* with warmth | *Ça va bien?* / *Bonne soirée, Sarah.* |
